approach: Build the drain fix-request work (it is not in this base) and answer the four findings. pin.rs turns the checker's reported problems into SourceFinding values (study, file, kind, statement, evidence, anchor). The anchor names the study entry that holds the statement: every string at any depth is credited to its nearest ancestor with an id, term or name (else its top-level key). Zero matches, or more than three, give a hash anchor. steward.rs builds one word-free marker 'Source fix: studies/<study>/<file> <kind> <anchor>', used as the request title and as the lookup key, plus the request text through StewardRequest::new and citing_request. drain.rs RealSteps::check_page queues one request per finding, skipping a finding when its request is open or its marker was already queued in this process for this repository. A drain run is one process, so that is at most one request per marker per run, even if the fix lands and the contradiction remains. Pass/fail and the Check detail do not change. c45 is re-cited from the pinned source if it can be read, else at the two already-validated reopen quotes, with the CHANGELOG saying what was not checked. model.json and intro.json are verified by Grep and edited only for a leftover.

decisions.choice: Queue a marker at most once per drain run with a process-wide set in drain.rs: `static SOURCE_FIX_QUEUED: Mutex<BTreeSet<(PathBuf, String)>>`, keyed by `athena.git.dir()` (athena-git lib.rs:198) and the marker. check_page checks and inserts under the lock before it calls `Athena::queue`, and removes the entry if the queue call fails. A finding is skipped when its marker is in the set or `citing_request` finds an open job. A request that closes (landed, failed or abandoned) therefore cannot cause another in the same run, and a later run (a new process) may queue it again.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The fix's own landing is an outcome landing (drain.rs:1814, OUTCOME_PATHS 462), so Drain::rate (2432-2451) runs check_page right after it. With 'open only' dedup a landed-but-ineffective fix would be re-queued, listed by steps.queue() (3084) and worked again, bounded only by budget. The run state lives in Drain, behind the Steps trait. A field on RealSteps would break about 40 struct literals, including tests/job_plan.rs:173 and tests/focus.rs:159, which are not deliverables. drain.rs already holds a static Mutex (TABLE_LOCK, 799), and every drain command builds its own RealSteps in one process (commands.rs:346, 371), so process scope is run scope. The path in the key keeps tests in one process apart (each Fixture has its own directory).

rejected.option: A field on RealSteps or Athena
rejected.why: Every struct literal of RealSteps (tests/drain.rs, job_plan.rs, focus.rs) and of Athena would need the new field. The change is far larger than the goal.

rejected.option: Treat only an open request as a duplicate (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The finding shows the loop: the fix lands, the rating is met, check_page runs and the same finding is queued again.

rejected.option: Never queue a marker that ever had a request, in any state
rejected.why: A failed or abandoned fix would never be asked for again, and a regression after a landed fix would never be queued, even in a later run.

rejected.option: Block re-queue when a closed request landed since the last change to the cited file
rejected.why: It needs per-file change history from git for each finding. The once-per-run set stops the loop with less code.

decisions.choice: finding_anchor walks the file's JSON with an 'owner' passed down. An object's owner is its own `id`, else `term`, else `name`. Otherwise it inherits the nearest ancestor's owner. A string with no owner above it takes its top-level key, if that is made of [A-Za-z0-9._-] and is at most 40 characters. An owner key that is not word-safe (a `name` sentence, a multi-word `term`) becomes 'n' plus 16 hex digits of the FNV-1a 64 of its normalised text. Every string value at any depth is a candidate except `id`, `term`, `name` values and `claims` arrays. A candidate matches when, after lowercasing, whitespace collapse and trimming quote marks, it contains the statement or is contained in it, the shorter side being at least 12 characters. The anchor is the sorted, de-duplicated owner keys of all matches joined with '+', when there are one to three of them. With no match, a non-JSON file, or more than three owners, the anchor is 'h' plus 16 hex digits of FNV-1a 64 of the normalised statement.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 4. model.json keeps text in nested objects without an id: t2's `retry.changes` (model.json:28-30), and `unhandled.failures` entries keyed by `name` only (model.json:119). Crediting descendants to the nearest owner makes the entry anchor those statements. A name-only entry gets a word-free hash of its own name, which is stable because the name is data, not model prose. The top-level key covers intro.json's `intro` and `transition` strings, which have no owner. More than three matches means the statement is broad, so the hash is used instead of an arbitrary three-id prefix; the rule goes in the doc comment.

rejected.option: Match only direct string fields of objects that have an id or term (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Nested model.json texts and name-keyed failures would fall back to the hash and be queued again.

rejected.option: Keep the first three sorted ids when more match
rejected.why: It is arbitrary, and the key then omits entries the statement touches.

rejected.option: Use a `name` sentence as the anchor text
rejected.why: It is not word-free, so the marker would go through boundary rewording and be unwieldy; its hash is stable and word-free.

rejected.option: Key on the statement text or the evidence
rejected.why: The model rewrites both between runs, so the same contradiction would be queued again.

decisions.choice: Build the marker once with `finding_marker` (through `plain_boundary_text`) and use that one string as both the request title passed to StewardRequest::new and the lookup key in `citing_request` and in the run set.
decisions.reason: StewardRequest::new rewords the title (steward.rs:544), so a raw marker could differ from the stored first line. A unit test checks that the rendered request's first line equals the marker.

rejected.option: Compare against a raw, un-reworded marker

risks.risk: The model paraphrases a statement so it matches no study entry, or quotes a different set of entries next run. The anchor then changes (hash, or another id set) and the same contradiction can be queued again in a later run.
risks.mitigation: Matching ignores case and spacing, accepts containment either way, and reaches nested strings. Evidence is not in the key. Within one run the once-per-run set bounds the cost, since it holds the marker, not the contradiction. A miss costs one extra request in a later run, never a wrong pass or fail. The CHANGELOG states the limit.

risks.risk: A landed fix that did not remove the contradiction is asked for again by the next drain run (one request per run), because a landed request is closed and so not open.
risks.mitigation: This is intended as a retry and is limited to one per marker per run. The held-back detail and the CHANGELOG say so. Blocking on 'ever landed' was rejected because it would hide a regression.

risks.risk: The process-wide set is hidden state, so the set persists for the life of the process and a test cannot reset it.
risks.mitigation: The key includes the repository directory, and each test Fixture has its own directory. The set only grows by one entry per queued marker. The doc comment on the static says it is the run scope.

risks.risk: Existing drain tests that run the real check with a failing fake checker now commit request records, which could change commit counts or Records assertions.
risks.mitigation: The commit happens only when the fake reports a problem, and only inside RealSteps::check_page. `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test` (criteria 4 and 6) are the check; tests/drain.rs is a deliverable and any assertion the new commit breaks is updated there.

risks.risk: c45 cannot be matched to a line that says Queued in this environment, so the real source check may flag c45 and queue one fix request on the next drain.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG says plainly that the cited lines do not say Queued and that the pinned source was not read. The Host question asks for the mount. With the once-per-run set and the open-request skip, that finding yields at most one request per run.

risks.risk: Queueing fails (a boundary word in a study or file name, a redaction change, a records commit error) and would abort the check.
risks.mitigation: The anchor is word-free (an id/term/key restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-], or h/n plus hex). The run set entry is removed when the queue call fails. A build or queue error is appended to the check detail and never changes pass or fail.

risks.risk: The model-backed check against the real pin cannot run here, so 'the drain source check passes on the corrected study' is not shown.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 3's demonstration records the route the conventions test prints and does not claim the source check ran. The CHANGELOG states which part was not run.

demonstrations.method: New drain tests in tests/drain.rs, all calling the production `RealSteps { athena, ui: &Quiet, page: &StubPage, lander }.check_page()` with a counting `SourceJudge` fake. Each builds its own claims.json through `commit_study` with its own files: c1 'Teardown closes a task, and a closed task can reopen.' and c2 'A worker slot is released when its pull request is ready.' (answers finding 2; the shared Texts claims.json has only c1). Test 1, `source_fix_queues_one_request_per_contradiction_and_none_while_open`: run 1 reports one `contradicted` problem on claims.json whose statement is a fragment of c1's text with no id and evidence 'pinned-source/bin/x.sh lines 30-33'. Run 2 reports the same fragment with different case and spacing and different evidence. Run 3 reports that problem plus a c2 fragment. Records are loaded at head after each run. Expected: one job whose first line is `Source fix: studies/demo/claims.json contradicted c1` after runs 1 and 2, and two after run 3, the second ending ` c2`. Run 1's text has the statement, the defanged evidence, an `Acceptance:` section and `Files: studies/demo/claims.json`; `request_text_touches` of it is only that file; `steward::citing_request` returns the job; the Check is still failed with `demo/claims.json` and the statement in its detail; and the production `steps.queue()` lists the job in items and plan with no open question (same-run pickup). Test 2, `source_fix_is_not_queued_again_after_its_job_lands_in_the_same_run` (finding 1): after run 1, a helper `close_request(fx, job, OutcomeState::Landed)` writes an `AnyRecord::Outcome` with `NewFile::record`, `write_bytes` and a commit, as seed_repeated_cause does at tests/drain.rs:4464-4519 and reconcile.rs:62 builds the Outcome. The fake still reports the contradiction and check_page runs again. Expected: still exactly one request job, none open, and `steps.queue()` does not list it. Test 3, `source_fix_closed_without_landing_is_queued_by_a_later_run_only`: in a fresh fixture, seed a request with `athena.queue(&source_fix_request(&finding))`, where the finding has anchor 'c1' and is built by hand, and close it as Failed. The first check_page then queues one new request, because this process has not queued the marker for this repository. Closing that one and calling check_page again queues none. Test 4: a 'did not report reading this file' problem queues nothing. Core unit tests: pin.rs `source_finding_*` and steward.rs `source_fix_*`. There is no refusal_corpus case: this is not a reading refusal or matching rule, and StewardRequest::new's checks are unchanged.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain source_fix && cargo test -p athena-core source_f && cargo test -p athena-cli && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: One request after run 1, still one after run 2 although case, spacing and evidence changed and no id was named, two after run 3. No second request after the first job lands with the contradiction still reported. A failed request is re-queued by a later run only. steps.queue() lists the new job. The pin and steward unit tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without dedup, run 2 makes a second request. With a key of file and kind only, run 3's c2 is skipped (count 1). With a key on evidence or the raw statement, run 2 makes a second request. With 'open only' dedup, test 2 finds a second request after the landed job. With no queueing, the count after run 1 is 0. With a raw marker, the unit test comparing it to the first line of the built request fails. With direct-fields-only matching, the nested-entry anchor test fails.
